items.title: In third season, Spurs' Stephon Castle receives high marks for 'maturity'
items.summary:
San Antonio Spurs Head Coach Mitch Johnson, left, talks with guard Stephon Castle during the second half of an NBA basketball game against the Chicago Bulls in Chicago, Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026. (AP Photo/Nam Y. Huh) (Nam Y. Huh/Associated Press)

With the shot clock winding down on a possession in the second period of the Spurs' 125-103 victory at Portland last week , Devin Vassell was forced to put up a hasty contested jumper from just inside the 3-point line.

The ball grazed the basket, went straight down onto the court and appeared to be headed out of bounds after a bounce when Stephon Castle swooped in to grab it in midair and fire it back to Vassell in one swift motion before falling in front of photographers sitting along the baseline.

Castle's hustling, heads-up save resulted in Vassell swishing a 3 from the corner for a seven-point lead.

Victor Wembanyama pumped in 29 points in just 24 minutes that night, but Spurs coach Mitch Johnson turned the post-game spotlight onto Castle. 

"Steph Castle took over the game there in the second quarter just in terms of the physicality and the competitiveness he played with and the execution and the poise and composure," Johnson said. "And our guys followed him."

Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are coming out of their Week 9 bye week at 6-2 overall and will battle for sole possession of first place in the AFC North on Sunday Night Football against the Cincinnati Bengals. Heading into the contest, Pittsburgh is in a good place health-wise.

Derrick Harmon is questionable for Sunday’s game after a full day of work. 

Ben Skowronek and others poised to return pic.twitter.com/OrKfTkbbzv 

— Mike DeFabo (@MikeDeFabo) November 13, 2026 After logging two limited practices to open the week and a full practice in Friday’s walkthrough, defensive tackle Derrick Harmon is listed as questionable to play on Sunday night. Earlier in the week, the Steelers opened up Harmon’s 21-day practice window, meaning he does not necessarily have to come back this week despite participating in practice throughout the week.

The young defensive lineman is the only name with a game designation on the Steelers’ Friday injury report. This means that the likes of Ben Skowronek, DeShon Elliott, Brandin Echols, and Donieko Slaughter are all good to go for the most important game of the season thus far.

Getting Harmon back on the field would be a huge boost to what has already been a strong Steelers defense in a high stakes matchup against the Bengals. The last time these two teams met, it was Harmon who clinched the game for the Steelers with a strip sack of Joe Burrow.

The Steelers will still be without wide receivers Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr., who remain on injured reserve.

items.title: Beachside surprise in FHSAA 3A boys golf as Christopher Grota tied for lead
items.summary:
St. Johns County teams Tocoi Creek and Beachside are in contention after the first round of the FHSAA Class 3A state boys golf tournament on Nov. 13 at the Mission Inn Resort El Campeon Course in Howey-in-the-Hills.

No surprise there.

What is a surprise is the individual at the top of the leaderboard: Beachside sophomore Christopher Grota, who had a hot front nine (El Campeon’s back, since he started at No. 10) and shot 4-under 68 to tie William Cui of Palm Beach Dwyer for first place.

Charlie Hipp of Creekside (69) is in third and Brady Dougan and Kaden James of Tocoi Creek (each at 72) are tied for seventh.

Dwyer leads the team standings at 2-under 290, with Beachside second, five shots behind and Tocoi Creek third, 14 back. They’re not out of it with one round to play on Nov. 14, especially if their No. 1 players reverse fortunes. Jaspreet Kondal of Beachside shot 74 and Ambrose Kinnare of Tocoi Creek made six bogeys on the front nine and shot 80.

Grota, who tied for fourth in District 2-3A (73) at Cimarrone and tied for seventh in Region 1-3A (72) at Cypress Head, birdied Nos. 14, 17 and 18 to turn at 3-under. He added a birdie at the par-3 second hole and was steady after that, closing with eight pars in a row.

Hipp, a senior who also began his round at No. 10, had three birdies, one eagle and two bogeys on the back, his front, then parred out on the front nine.

items.title: Edge Tyson Williams cuts list to 10; Kentucky still in the hunt
items.summary:
When 30 programs want the same 6-foot-4, 240-pound disruptor, the hard part isn’t the offers. It’s the subtraction.

Tyson Williams , the 4-star edge from Shelby (N.C.) and the No. 28 edge in the 2028 class per Rivals, has done that math. The pile of suitors is now a list of 10: South Carolina, North Carolina , SMU, Louisville, Kentucky , Tennessee, Auburn, Alabama , Miami, and Virginia Tech.

The names are loud. The reason they made the cut is quiet.

What has kept all of these schools in the hunt for me has really just been consistent communication and love from the coaches and staff. I feel it heavy with all of them, so that’s really who I’m going to try to focus on. 

In recruiting, that is the whole game, played on a phone screen at odd hours. Williams isn’t talking about a flashy pitch or a facility tour. He’s talking about who keeps showing up in the notifications, and the ten schools on his list all have.

Kentucky has made it with a coach and a trajectory, and Williams has noticed both. The No. 13 Wildcats have been on the climb under Will Stein, and the 2028 prospects who are watching have taken notes.

They have really turned things around, and I believe completely that Coach Stein is making a name for football at Kentucky .

That is a recruit’s version of a scouting report on a program: not the record, but the direction. A defensive force who lives in the backfield wants to know where a program is headed before he decides where to be, and Williams sees Lexington as a place that is going somewhere.

What he wants from here is simple. He wants the communication…
items.t: Edge Tyson Williams cuts list to 10; Kentucky still in the hunt

items.title: Cummins stands firm on ball tampering to leave Australian cricket back where it started | Geoff Lemon
items.summary:
The Test captain kept his promise to answer all questions at a press conference that made his position clear and filled some but not all gaps

Our coverage on Thursday said that Pat Cummins needed to front up, and nobody can fairly say that he didn’t. It was a proper ’til-they-drop affair from Australia’s cricket captain, an hour and 10 minutes at a press conference podium taking questions about the 2018 ball-tampering episode until every journalist present ran out of steam. You might have expected some partial concession to teammate Usman Khawaja’s depiction of endemic cheating, but Cummins was firm that this did not reflect the life he’d known. Once more with feeling, but more importantly with detail.

Media accounts will now depict this as Cummins and Khawaja at war, because a falling-out among friends is a juicy story to fatten up and serve for gluttony. It isn’t fair, because both have emphasised the importance of their friendship, strained as it must now be. As two thoughtful people with shared history, they have a better chance than most to find a way through.

items.title: NFL quarterbacks are under more pressure than ever from rushers. Why?
items.summary:
Despite all the advantages offenses have secured over the years, defenses are better at pressuring the QB than any other time in recent history

The Baltimore Ravens are preparing to start their fourth quarterback this year, Jacoby Brissett, against the beleaguered Los Angeles Chargers on Monday, because of injuries to Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley and Joe Fagnano. That puts them dangerously close to the NFL record of five within a single season (a record shared by the 1984 Bears and 2023 Browns when excluding the 1987 strike season).

Jackson, Huntley and Fagnano were all injured after taking hits in games. And if it seems like quarterbacks are taking punishment more often this year, your eyes aren’t deceiving you. Through nine weeks, quarterbacks have been hit on 15.1% of their dropbacks, the most we’ve seen since 2006, when hits were first logged in official box scores.

items.title: The beautiful game: revived art prize gives football its creative due once more | Emma John
items.summary:
Football and the art world have long remained distant but the breadth of entries for this year’s award reveals a healthy revival

It may be the Beautiful Game, but in its early decades football was a rare subject for artists. The Italian Futurist Umberto Boccioni whirled an athlete’s body into a vortex of movement in his 1913 painting Dynamism of a Soccer Player. You can see one of the earliest fine art depictions of a match – a smoggy, factory-adjactent scene called Any Wintry Afternoon in England – at the Manchester Art Gallery. If 1930s abstraction is more your thing, you can enjoy decoding the geometric shapes in Kazimir Malevich’s Painterly Realism of a Football Player – Color Masses in the 4th Dimension. I’m guessing the small green pea shape is a ball.

These, in any case, were exceptions. In 1953 the Football Association launched an art prize, backed by the newly formed Arts Council: the winning works included Going To The Match by LS Lowry, with its crowds flocking to Bolton Wanderers’ then home ground, Burnden Park. An exhibition of the submissions, Football and The Fine Arts, toured the country and the FA secretary, Sir Stanley Rous, said he hoped it would finally break the barrier between those two worlds.

items.title: It’s Happy Harry Kane day as England’s finest seizes his moment in style | Barney Ronay
items.summary:
The Ballon d’Or validated the forward’s career and he extended his incredible record for England with yet another goal on his 126th appearance

Happy Harry Kane day! And many happy Harry returns. There is a process in clinical psychology known as semantic satiation. Subjects are asked to repeat a word or phrase so many times that it loses any kind of meaning. Suddenly “daffodils” is just an absurd, empty set of sounds. So it was in the buildup to Harry Kane’s record-breaking 126th cap, at the end of Harry Kane Ballon d’Or fortnight, as Harry Kane’s England were led out by top scorer Harry Kane, climax to a week of Harry Kane tributes, Harry Kane montages, 26-page Harry Kane … wait. Where were we?

This was that kind of occasion from start to finish, a night where you expected to look up from your desk mid-match to see Kane’s head looming helpfully over your shoulder, to enter the Wembley toilets at half-time and find him silently offering you a breath mint and a scented tissue.
